text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told reporters Monday that the biggest problems facing the country today are the state of law and order, opportunities for job starters and the insufficient support extended to civil organizations.
- Parliament will likely vote next Tuesday on two new nominees to the vacancies on the Constitutional Court.

- Free Democrat House leader Istvan Szent-Ivanyi and his party MPs yesterday presented reports from the screening committee showing that none of them worked in any capacity for the secret service during the communist era.
- Three opposition parties Monday appealed to President Arpad Goncz to refer to the Constitutional Court last week's amendment to the law on the administration of social insurance authorities.
- The Smallholders parliamentary group yesterday decided not to support an initiative to call a referendum regarding a planned amendment to the land law.

- Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec advocated cooperation with Hungary in the two countries' efforts to gain membership in Euro-Atlantic organizations, during his one-day visit to Hungary Monday.
- Hungarian exports to the US will again be treated under the generalized system of preferences (GSP) from autumn, according to Ferenc Furulyas Hungary's trade counsel in Washington.

- National Radio and Television Board (ORTT) spokesman Gyorgy Lovas said Monday that ORTT will announce the results of a tender for concession rights to broadcasting on two commercial TV channels around June 24-26.
-The US credit-rating agency Duff & Phelps announced that it has upgraded Hungary's foreign currency debts to BBB+ from BBB-.
- Agriculture is not expected to achieve a quick or permanent boom, according to analysts of the economic research company GKI.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- EU Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler said Monday that Hungary ranks third in suitability for EU membership after the Czech Republic and Slovenia, and is followed by Slovakia and Poland.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- According to the 1998 budget proposal being worked out by the Finance Ministry, ministries and local councils will be able to spend 5% more on materials and 14.5% more on wages next year.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The brake system components manufacturer Knorr-Bremse plans to develop its Kecskemet plant into its largest unit in Europe.

- French novelist Robert Merle's passport expired Sunday and he had to wait several hours before the French authorities issued another one allowing him to arrive in Hungary yesterday to sign books at the Helikon book shop in Budapest.
